summary: Master logistics technology, telematics and fleet analytics through KPI dashboards, route diagnostics, and practical fleet reporting. Enrol today.
lede: Fleet analytics training helps transport, logistics, and dispatch professionals turn vehicle and route data into practical operational decisions. Participants learn to check and integrate telematics data, define KPIs for utilization, delivery, fuel use, and maintenance, and diagnose exceptions such as route deviations and idling. They also practice building fleet dashboards and translating findings into dispatch, maintenance, and optimization actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who work directly with fleet movement, telematics outputs, transport reporting, and operational control. It suits you if you need to improve daily visibility, interpret vehicle data, or turn fleet analytics into practical action in a transport, logistics, or distribution setting. Fleet Supervisors who monitor vehicle movement, utilisation, and daily exceptions. Transport Planners who align routes, schedules, and capacity with service demand. Logistics Analysts who clean telematics data and build fleet KPI reports. Dispatch Coordinators who manage route changes, delays, and escalation workflows. Maintenance Planners who use telematics signals for preventive servicing decisions. Operations Managers who oversee fleet cost, service, and control tower performance. Transport Controllers who track adherence, exceptions, and same-day corrective action. Fleet Performance Analysts who diagnose fuel, idle, and utilisation variance. Supply Chain Analysts who connect transport data to service and cost outcomes. Logistics Technology Coordinators who support telematics adoption and reporting governance.
prerequisites: Participants should bring a laptop and be prepared to work in Microsoft Excel for calculations and basic data review. If available, you may also bring example telematics exports, GPS reports, fleet KPI summaries, or transport management system extracts from your own role for practical exercises.
